messages:
Maya: quick run notes — I ran a family of KV-cache microbenchmarks across regions to stress the eviction/prefetch tradeoffs. us-east1(H100), eu-west1(A100), apac1(H100s). traces: chat-mix (slen median 128), longform (slen median 1024), and spike (10% > 2k).

Maya: goal = map hit_rate -> p99 token latency under different prefetch windows (0, 8, 32) and eviction thresholds (LRU window sizes 64k, 256k, 1M entries). small configs used 8-bit quantized weights, same model blob.

Maya: command I used (for reproducibility):
```
./bench_kv --trace=traces/chat-mix.json --gpu=h100 --region=us-east1 --prefetch=32 --lru=256k --out=run_us_east_prefetch32_lru256k.csv
```

Evan: nice. what were the key metrics you captured?

Maya: captured stats per token request: cache_hit(bool), latency_ms, kernel (matmul/path), seq_len, kv_page_faults, cpu_to_gpu_copy_ms. summarized as hit_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and tail page fault rate (>0.1ms).

Priya: can you paste a short table for chat-mix vs longform? just p99 and hit_rate for the interesting configs.

Maya: here — condensed (hit_rate, p99_ms) for prefetch=0 / 8 / 32 with LRU=256k on us-east1(H100):
- chat-mix (median 128): prefetch=0 -> (0.62, 48); prefetch=8 -> (0.78, 34); prefetch=32 -> (0.82, 30)
- longform (median 1024): prefetch=0 -> (0.29, 210); prefetch=8 -> (0.52, 120); prefetch=32 -> (0.59, 98)

Maya: same longform on eu-west1(A100) with prefetch=32 LRU=256k: (0.57, 112) — slight kernel difference (A100 running different matmul kernels) increased p99 ~14% vs H100 for the same hit_rate.

Luca: interesting. so prefetch window clearly helps more for long sequences (cache warmup). did you see any cases where prefetch made tail worse because of contention?

Maya: yes — on apac1(H100s) with high concurrency (200 qps), prefetch=32 + LRU=1M caused occasional CPU->GPU micro-bursts leading to small page fault spikes. Example: spike trace (10% >2k): prefetch=32 had hit_rate 0.72 but p99 jumped to 260ms vs prefetch=8 p99=210ms. So large prefetch + large LRU increases scheduling contention in that region under heavy burst workloads.

Priya: do we have any kernel-level breakdown for the worst p99s? maybe a single matmul kernel or memcpy dominating?

Maya: yes — I profiled the hot tails. For the bad apac run, 65% of extra latency came from `kv_page_pop` on the memcpy path (host->device) and 25% from a fallback matmul kernel that runs slower at long seqlen (kernel id: mm_long_emu).

Evan: suggestion: add a soft prefetch throttler that drops prefetches when device queue depth > X. That should mitigate the bursts while keeping average hit_rate.

Luca: agree. also consider regional kernel hints: prefer A100-optimized kernels for eu-west, H100-specific ones in us-east/apac. We can add kernel-pinning as a per-region config.

Priya: any recommendation for default config for hosted customers? something conservative to avoid apac spikes but still good hit_rate for longform?

Maya: for now recommend: prefetch=8, LRU=256k. That hits a good mid point: chat-mix p99 ~34ms, longform p99 ~120ms in most regions. For dedicated customers we can expose `prefetch` and `prefetch_throttle_qd` knobs.

ciara-bot: automated note: created bench-ticket #ML-1221 to track prefetch-throttle + kernel-pinning action items. Assigned to @Maya and @Luca.

Evan: SGTM. can you drop the raw csvs in the benchmark bucket? I'll run the cost model on the per-token latency delta vs hit rate.

Maya: uploading to s3://redwood-bench/kv/1754329876/ now (files: run_us_east_prefetch32_lru256k.csv, run_eu_prefetch32_lru256k.csv, run_apac_spike_prefetch32_lru1m.csv).

Luca: follow-up tests to run: (1) prefetch=16, throttle_qd=64 across regions, (2) same traces with mixed quant (int8 int4) to see kernel fallback rate. I'll schedule today.

Priya: thanks Maya — super helpful. can you add a one-paragraph summary to the ticket with the conservative defaults?

Maya: will do. tl;dr at top of ticket: default prefetch=8, lru=256k, enable throttle at qd>=64.

Evan: :thumbsup:
